Judgment

1. This is an appeal petition preferred by the State ( prosecution agency before Ld. Trial Court)
against the impugned order dated 16.03.2022 passed by the court of Ms. Dhanshree Deka, Ld.
Metropolitan Magistrate, Rohini Courts, Delhi in case FIR No. 209/2006, under Section 498-A IPC of P.S Adarsh Nagar, titled as 'State V. Jitender, whereby the respondent (accused before the Ld.
Trial Court) has been acquitted.
2.
The facts in brief as per the charge-sheet are that the marriage between the respondent herein and de - facto complainant Sheetal Thareja was solemnized 28.02.2001 as per Hindu Rites and Ceremonies.
The complainant alleged that she never lived peacefully after the marriage and there were quarrels in the joint family of her husband (respondent herein).
After the death of her father-in-law, property dispute arose between her husband and other family members.
Her husband(respondent herein) was separated from work.
She was harassed by family members of respondent herein.
Her in-laws used to raise dowry demand and used to taunt her for not bringing dowry.
The complainant further alleged that her brother-in-law used to instigate her husband (respondent herein) to beat her.
On 01.01.2005, the complainant was driven out of matrimonial home by her in-laws as there was property dispute in the family.
2.1 Later on, one settlement took place between the parties and Rs.10 lacs were given to the complainant and her husband (respondent herein) for purchasing of separate house.

Thereafter,
complainant and respondent herein shifted to another house.
The complainant further alleged that her brother-in-law (Jeth) and his wife (Jethani) got signature of accused on certain documents.

She also alleged that when she asked the respondent for her belongings, she was beaten up and harassed State vs Jitender S/O Late Sh. Thakur Dass on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9050160/
1 by respondent.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She lodged a complaint against her in-laws on 01.07.2005.

2.2 After the completion of the investigation of the case, chargesheet was filed and matter was put on trial against accused persons namely Ramesh, Vijay, Seema, Sunita, Asha, Santosh and Jitender (petitioner herein) for the offence u/s 498A/34 IPC.
After conclusion of the trial, Ld. MM acquitted the accused ( respondent herein ) of the offence punishable under Section 498A IPC vide impugned judgment.

3. That feeling aggrieved by the said impugned judgment the State/Appellant has challenged the same on the following grounds :
a. That the impugned order passed by Ld. M.M is based on conjectures and surmises.

b. That the Ld. MM has failed to appreciate the testimony of PW-1 who is the complainant wherein she has made specific allegations against her husband and her in-laws that they had raised dowry demand during her pregancy stating that it is the custom to give jewellery articles on the birth of baby in their family.
c. That the Ld. MM has overlooked the fact that PW-1 made further allegations of beating against her husband in 2002.
She also alleged that her husband was beating her and her mother-in-law was pushing her neck and her Jethani Sunita was watching the whole incident silently and did not come to save her.

Further, the Ld.
MM failed to consider that PW-1 alleged that respondent raised demand of Rs.10,000/- and also he (respondent) used to consume excessive liquor and give her beatings.
On 06.05.2009 at about 5:30 p.m, accused (respondent) pulled her hair so hard that front part of her hair came off.
d. That the judgment of Ld. MM is not in accordance with well settled principles of law on "beyond reasonable doubt" as laid down in case AIR 2002 SC 3633.
4. Reply to the appeal has been filed by the respondent.

5. The Ld. Addl P.P for the petitioner/State, in support of the said grounds, further argued that the Ld. Trial Court while acquitting the accused/respondent herein has totally ignored the version given by the complainant Ms. Sheetal Thareja (PW-1) and the Ld. Trial Court has simplicitor relied upon the version given by the defence witness namely Ramesh Kumar (DW-1).
There is no reason to discard the credible and trustworthy version of complainant Ms. Sheetal Thareja (PW-1) who is the victim in the present case.
6. Per contra, Ld. Counsel for the respondent has argued that there is no legal infirmity in the impugned order of the Ld Trial Court which calls for any interference.
The Ld. Trial Court passed the impugned judgment after considering the facts on record, analyzing the versions of material witnesses.

It is further argued that it is a case of property dispute only and wife of the accused /respondent herein complainant Ms. Sheetal Thareja (PW-1) wanted to grab the property of State vs Jitender S/O Late Sh. Thakur Dass on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9050160/
2 respondent which has been proved on record.
The house which was bought out of the amount of Rs.10 lacs given as settlement amount to both of them is under the occupation and possession of said complainant Ms. Sheetal Thareja (PW-1) only.
The respondent herein has been thrown out of the said house despite it being in joint name.
7. I have heard the Ld. Addl. PP for the State and Ld. Counsel for the respondent and considered the material placed on record.
8. Before appreciating the rival contentions of the parties, it would be appropriate if the sequence of the events in the present case are appreciated.

The FIR in question was got registered consequent to the lodging of handwritten complaint dated 28.02.2026 of Ms. Sheetal Thareja (PW-1) which is a detailed complaint addressed to DCP, CAW Cell, Pitam Pura, Delhi.
The preliminary inquiry was got conducted and after the preliminary inquiry , the FIR was got registered.

Initially the charge-sheet was filed against respondent herein as well as his family members namely Ramesh, Vijay, Seema,
Sunita, Asha and Santosh.
But the Ld. Trial Court vide its order on charge dated 17.11.2016 discharged the remaining family members finding not sufficient ground to proceed against them.
The said order of discharge has not been challenged by the prosecution .The

charge under Section 498A IPC was framed against the respondent herein/husband of complainant Ms. Sheetal Thareja (PW-1) and the prosecution in order to prove the said charge has primarily placed reliance upon the version by PW-1 and Ms. Chanderkanta (PW-4) who is the mother of complainant Sheetal Thareja (PW-1).
9.

The crux of the arguments advanced on behalf of the appellant herein is that Ld. Trial Court while acquitting the accused/respondent herein has given undue importance to the version of Defence Witness namely Ramesh Kumar (DW-1) and thereby ignoring the version of victim/complainant Ms. Sheetal Thareja (PW-1) despite her version regarding she being harassed, assaulted and tortured by the accused/respondent herein on account of insufficient dowry or demand of dowry.

10. Ms. Sheetal Thareja (PW-1) in her deposition in Court which runs into 21 pages has given narration of entire incidents involving the cruelty right since the marriage i.e 28.02.2001 till the time she left the matrimonial home and filed the complaint i.e 01.07.2005.

As far as the various instances of subsequent incidents of harassment narrated by her in her examination-in-chief which took place between the year 2006 to 2009 are concerned, the same cannot considered in the present case being not part of the charges framed against the respondent herein.
11. The only limited question which requires to be considered is as to whether the version of said PW-1 reiterating the said incidents of harassment inspire confidence or not.
The sum and substance of her version recorded in the Court reflects that allegations of cruelty on account of insufficient dowry or demands of dowry are primarily against the in-laws.

Inter alia, her version rather reflects her grievance that her husband (respondent herein) too is being the victim of acts of remaining in laws as they deprived him of his rights in the joint family property or the business run by them.

State vs Jitender S/O Late Sh. Thakur Dass on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9050160/
3 12.
The first incident of harassment qua the demand of dowry concerns somewhere the time when she gave birth to her first daughter.
She deposed that during pregnancy her aforesaid in-laws raised demand of giving jewelery articles as it is their custom and she was harassed in this regard.
The said term 'in-law' used by her has to be seen in the light of the version given in the initial part of her examination-in-chief.

She clarified that her in-law i.e her mother-in-law, both sisters-in-law namely Seema and Sunita, her brother-in-law namely Ramesh and Vijay and their wives namely Santosh and Asha used to harass her and they used to instigate her husband (respondent herein) in the harassment.
13.
So, it has been rightly observed by the Ld. Trial Court that the first incident of harassment and demand of dowry does not concern the respondent herein.

PW1 further clarified the role of the respondent and other in-laws vis-a-vis the family affairs and her harassment in following part of her deposition which is reproduced:
"all the aforesaid in-laws started cursing me for giving birth to a girl child.
They also cursed me by saying that I had taken life of my father-in-law after setting foot in my matrimonial home.
During the pregancy, all the aforesaid in-laws raised the demand of jewellery items to be given on the birth of child.
They told that it is their custom to give jewellery to the in-laws at the birth of the child, so I must fulfil their demand."

13.1 Thus the said part of her testimony reflects the major role played by the in-laws in her harassment and her testimony rather exonerates the respondent herein of any harassment on account of demand of dowry.

14. The second incident alleged by Ms. Sheetal Thareja (PW-1) is concerning the time when the respondent herein went for Kawar Yatra (a religious travel undertaken by people during the month of Spring /Sawan) and he did not return on time.
The search of respondent herein was carried out by her and thereafter when he returned , the behaviour of her husband became unusual and he started misbehaving.
He pretended to be under the control of some ghost.

The said part of the testimony of Ms. Sheetal Thareja (PW-1) does not help the case of the prosecution as the same does not in any manner connect the respondent herein with the allegations of cruelty in connections with the demand of dowry etc.
15.
Another specific incident deposed by her took place in September 2002 when her husband (respondent herein) and her mother-in-law pushed her as they wanted to kill her.

Again, the said incident does not in any manner show the allegations accused/respondent herein having instigated her mother-in-law or the said allegations having any connection with the demand of dowry raised by her other in laws and he being party to the allegations of demand of dowry raised by her other in-laws.
16. The next specific instance narrated by her is demand of Rs.10,000/- which took place somewhere around November 2003.

As far as the said demand is concerned, she (PW-1) deposed as under:
State vs Jitender S/O Late Sh. Thakur Dass on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9050160/
4

entities.text: State vs Jitender S/O Late Sh. Thakur Dass
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "My husband said to me that his brother demanded of Rs.10,000/- to bring from my parental home.
I asked my husband that I don't have any money, ask your brother to pay the complete bill and we shall pay the same in installments."

17. So, the intent behind the said part of her deposition is quite apparent that her husband (respondent herein) was in no manner raising the demand rather as per own version only, the other in-laws were pressuring her husband to communicate it and her husband was also being tortured in this regard.
The said part of the testimony also exonerates the respondent herein of the charges levelled as has been rightly observed and appreciated by the Ld. Trial Court.

18. The last material part of the allegations concerns the beating given by the accused /respondent herein under the influence of liquor and the said beatings having even continued after July 2005 when they both moved out of the matrimonial home and started residing in their separate home at B-213, Indira Nagar.
19. As far as the said allegations are concerned, again they are not concerning the demand of dowry raised by the respondent herein.

Rather it is a material improvement made by the complainant qua settlement between the family involving her husband and his brothers which completely demolishes the case of the prosecution against the respondent and other family members .

The factum of compromise which took place between the parties was deposed by the witness Ms. Sheetal Thareja (PW-1) as under :
"Then, I came back to my parental home.
The matter was compromised between my husband and his brothers and they gave my husband Rs.10 lacs to move out of my matrimonial house.
Me and my husband moved out of the matrimonial house and my husband bought a house for Rs.7 lacs 5 thousand in our joint names.
Rs.95,000/- was kept in cash to FD of Rs.50,000/- each were done in our combined names.
I was told that the FD was in name of my daughters.
Another Rs.50,000/- was deposited in Post Office in both our names and the balance amount of Rs.50,000/- in Post Office by accused in his own name.
My husband was still doing work in family business with is brothers.
He also bought a Maruti Car for a sum of Rs.60,000/- which he sold after a month.
He used to regularly drink with my Jeth who used to come to our house.
My Jeth used to instigate my husband to hit me."
20. So, as per Ms. Sheetal Thareja ( PW-1), they were given Rs.10 lacs as settlement amount for moving out of the matrimonial home somewhere in July2005.

The major part of the said amount i.e 7.5 lacs was utilized for buying a house in the joint name of both husband and wife (respondent herein and complainant respectively) and remaining amount was kept in the form of FD or cash,
that too was in the joint name.
Apart from that, she further deposed that on the instigation of her Jeth ( husband's elder brother) only, her husband (respondent herein) used to drink and hit her.

20.1 The said part of her version rather probablises the defence of accused/respondent that the present case is outcome of property dispute only and is an attempt to grab the said joint property which was purchased out of the settlement amount in their joint name.

Though PW-1 in her cross-examination tried to retract from her said admission by claiming that for purchase of said State vs Jitender S/O Late Sh. Thakur Dass on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9050160/
5 house for a sum of Rs.7.05 lacs, Rs 2.50 lacs were contributed by her parents on the demand of her in-laws and accused/respondent herein.

entities.text: State vs Jitender S/O Late Sh. Thakur Dass
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She further claimed that the said amount was paid in cash.
The said fact contribution of Rs.2.50 lacs has been reiterated by Ms. Chanderkanta (PW-4).
Though she in her cross-examination stated that the said amount was paid by way of cheque, but does not remember the cheque number.
She was not even able to disclose the exact date, month or year when the said demand was raised.
Therefore the said part of her allegations has been rightly discarded by the Ld Trial Court .

20.2 PW-4 rather contradicted the entire case of the prosecution as well as that of complainant/PW1 by claiming that accused, right since the beginning of the marriage, was raising the demand of house and car from them.
Admittedly, as per the record and the version given by PW-1, no such demand was raised by the accused at any point of time.
Rather, she claimed that there was no harassment or any demand till the time, her father was alive.

In these circumstances, not much credence can be attached to the versions given by both PW-1 and PW-4 and has rightly been discarded by the Ld.
Trial Court.
21.
Now, coming to the other argument advanced on behalf of the State/Appellant that undue importance has been given to the version of Ramesh Kumar (DW-1).
It is the well settled proposition of law that witnesses, be that of prosecution or defence stand on the same pedestal.

The veracity and truthfulness of the witnesses has to be judged and appreciated which has been rightly done so by the Ld. Trial Court in believing the version of some of crucial aspects as deposed by DW-1.
The version of DW-1 qua lodging of the complaints of harassment by PW-1 vide Ex.DW-1/A to Ex.DW-1/A- 3 is not rebutted or challenged on behalf of the State/Appellant.
The other aspect is the the factum of settlement between the parties and Rs.10 lacs being given as settlement amount to the respondent and the complainant Ms. Sheetal Thareja (PW-1).
Even no suggestion denying the said fact has been given on behalf of the State/Appellant.

Therefore the Ld Trial Court rightly believed the version given by the DW1 which demolishes the case of prosecution and version of PW1.She still continuous to be in occupation of house purchased through settlement amount paid by her in-laws.
The respondent is residing separately as has been admitted by PW-1 in her cross which shows the falsity of her allegations of demand of dowry.

23. In view of the above-discussed reasons and observations, I am of the considered opinion that there is no legal infirmity or irregularity in the impugned judgment passed by the Ld. Trial Court which needs to be interfered.
Therefore, the impugned judgment is upheld hereby and the appeal of the appellant/State is dismissed.
There is no order as to cost.
TCR be sent back with a copy of this order.
Appeal file be consigned to Record Room.
